symbol_descriptions: Instantaneous rate of change of population abundance under delayed density-dependent crowding with high-abundance compression of abundance-amplified realized competition
Strength of crowding-mediated suppression per unit abundance and crowding-pressure state
Scale controlling saturation of incremental crowding damage at high crowding-pressure state
Rate at which abundance generates crowding pressure
Rate at which crowding pressure dissipates
Coefficient controlling extra realized crowding loss that grows with abundance at fixed latent crowding pressure
Nonnegative coefficient introducing stronger-than-hyperbolic compression of additional crowding damage at high latent crowding
Nonnegative compression scale causing the abundance-amplified competition factor to bend over at high abundance

new_symbol_range_suggestions.abundance_amplification_compression: nonnegative; typically small enough that abundance_amplification_compression*N << 1 at low-to-moderate abundance but order one when abundance_crowding_curvature*N is order one or larger

derivation_notes: The parent assumed the abundance-amplified competition factor stayed exactly linear in N for all admissible abundance. Here that factor is refined to a saturating form so extra individuals still increase realized competition at fixed C, but with diminishing marginal effect once competitive exposure overlaps strongly at high abundance.
change_summary: I changed the assumption that abundance-driven amplification of competition is unsaturating. The crowding-loss coefficient now depends nonlinearly on N through a high-abundance compression scale, creating observable curvature in dN_dt versus N at fixed moderate-to-high C.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: The extra realized crowding loss factor (1 + abundance_crowding_curvature*N) is an unsaturating linear function of abundance for all biologically admissible N.
assumption_audit.mechanism: At very high abundance, repeated encounters, shared depleted neighborhoods, or limited contact surface make additional individuals less able to create fresh independent competitive exposure, so abundance-amplified realized competition still grows with N but with diminishing marginal effect.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: The successor reduces to the parent when abundance_amplification_compression -> 0, giving 1 + abundance_crowding_curvature*N/(1 + abundance_amplification_compression*N) -> 1 + abundance_crowding_curvature*N over the admissible range.

response_change.parent_relation: At fixed latent crowding pressure C, crowding loss enters as competition_strength*C*N*(1 + abundance_crowding_curvature*N) divided by a saturation function of C only, so the realized per-capita suppression is affine in N for any given C.
response_change.child_relation: At fixed C, the abundance-amplified realized competition should itself compress at high N because encounter overlap or local depletion cannot keep increasing quadratically without bound once most individuals are already exposed; this changes the N-to-dN_dt mapping from affine to subquadratically curved at high abundance.
response_change.observable_effect: When C is moderate-to-high and N spans low to high values along the trajectory, the child predicts that increasingly large N increments cause smaller additional decreases in dN_dt than the parent's fixed linear-in-N per-capita amplification, while still preserving monotone crowding damage.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable when abundance_amplification is order one or larger and latent_crowding_load is not negligible, i.e. N becomes large enough along the realized trajectory that the current linear abundance amplification would otherwise overstate incremental suppression; weak effect when abundance_crowding_curvature*N << 1.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, the mechanism appears as mild deviation from linear abundance amplification during periods of elevated C; in holdout with larger realized N at similar viable parameters, the same compression becomes clearer as dN_dt decreases more slowly than the parent predicts at the highest abundances.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit where the new high-abundance compression scale tends to zero effect, so the abundance-dependent factor returns to 1 + abundance_crowding_curvature*N over the admissible range.
evolution_contract.domain_mechanism: high-abundance compression of abundance-amplified realized competition
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: At very high abundance, repeated encounters, shared depleted neighborhoods, or limited contact surface make additional individuals less able to create fresh independent competitive exposure, so abundance-amplified realized competition still grows with N but with diminishing marginal effect.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This is harder than a coefficient-only correction because the effective coefficient of the existing crowding-loss branch now varies with N, changing the shape of the target mapping across the trajectory rather than merely rescaling loss uniformly.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: The extra realized crowding loss factor (1 + abundance_crowding_curvature*N) is an unsaturating linear function of abundance for all biologically admissible N.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: The abundance-amplified realized crowding factor compresses at high abundance, remaining monotone but with diminishing marginal amplification.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: Compare epochs or parameter settings where latent_crowding_load is moderate-to-high while N sweeps from low to high along the same trajectory. The parent gives an affine abundance amplification inside the crowding term at fixed C, whereas the child bends over so dN_dt becomes less negative than the parent would predict at the largest N, without changing the low-N limit.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set cannot generally match both the low-N and high-N parts of this mapping under similar C because its abundance-amplified competition factor is structurally linear in N. Retuning competition_strength or abundance_crowding_curvature can change gain, but cannot create the child’s high-N bending while preserving the same lower-N slope under the same moderate-to-high crowding regime.

evolution_plan.activation_condition: Observable when abundance_amplification is order one or larger and latent_crowding_load is not negligible, i.e. N becomes large enough along the realized trajectory that the current linear abundance amplification would otherwise overstate incremental suppression; weak effect when abundance_crowding_curvature*N << 1.
evolution_plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, the mechanism appears as mild deviation from linear abundance amplification during periods of elevated C; in holdout with larger realized N at similar viable parameters, the same compression becomes clearer as dN_dt decreases more slowly than the parent predicts at the highest abundances.
evolution_plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit where the new high-abundance compression scale tends to zero effect, so the abundance-dependent factor returns to 1 + abundance_crowding_curvature*N over the admissible range.
evolution_plan.gap_statement: The parent assumes abundance-driven amplification of competition keeps increasing linearly in N at fixed latent crowding pressure, with no high-abundance compression of that amplification.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: The extra realized crowding loss factor (1 + abundance_crowding_curvature*N) is an unsaturating linear function of abundance for all biologically admissible N.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: At very high abundance, repeated encounters, shared depleted neighborhoods, or limited contact surface make additional individuals less able to create fresh independent competitive exposure, so abundance-amplified realized competition still grows with N but with diminishing marginal effect.
evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the parent's fixed linear abundance amplification within the already present crowding-loss mechanism, not to add a new biological process. Vary N along the continuous trajectory while holding the same parameter set and comparing epochs with similar moderate-to-high C. In the parent, at fixed C the slope of suppression with respect to N keeps strengthening linearly through the factor 1 + abundance_crowding_curvature*N, so dN_dt becomes increasingly more negative with essentially constant second derivative contribution from that branch. In the child, that abundance amplification bends over at high N, giving a measurable curvature change in the target mapping dN_dt(N,C): suppression remains monotone but the marginal extra loss from further abundance increments shrinks once many individuals already share the same crowding field. This is scientifically admissible under the given closed-population crowding scenario and does not violate the constraint that crowding must not increase per-capita net growth. The contrast is observable only if the realized trajectory reaches abundance_crowding_curvature*N of order one or larger; otherwise the parent and child are practically indistinguishable. A single refit of existing parent parameters cannot generally reproduce both the early-N and late-N curvature under the same C regime, because the parent is structurally affine in N within the abundance-amplified competition factor and can only change its overall gain, not introduce high-N bending without disturbing lower-N behavior.

selected_embedding_pattern.description: Make the coefficient of an existing process depend on a declared quantity.

scenario_text: Track a closed population whose abundance changes through reproduction and background mortality while crowding progressively suppresses net growth. At low abundance, the population should increase approximately in proportion to its size, whereas near a finite environmental limit its net change should approach zero. The target is the instantaneous rate of abundance change over a single continuous trajectory.
